items.stem: President Warren G. Harding's and President Calvin Coolidge's tax programme cut the top income tax rate from 73 percent to 25 percent across the 1920s. Which official designed it and served both presidents as Secretary of the Treasury?
items.stemEs: El programa fiscal de los presidentes Warren G. Harding y Calvin Coolidge redujo la tasa máxima del impuesto sobre la renta del 73 por ciento al 25 por ciento a lo largo de los años veinte. ¿Qué funcionario lo diseñó y sirvió a ambos presidentes como secretario del Tesoro?

choices.text: Charles G. Dawes, who held budget office under Harding and later served as Coolidge's vice president
choices.textEs: Charles G. Dawes, que ocupó un cargo presupuestario bajo Harding y luego sirvió como vicepresidente de Coolidge
choices.explanation: Both halves are true. Dawes was the first Director of the Bureau of the Budget in 1921 and Coolidge's vice president from 1925, and he never ran the Treasury: the budget bureau controlled federal spending, not tax rates.
choices.misconception: swaps the official who controlled spending for the one who set tax rates

choices.text: Herbert Hoover, who served in the cabinet under both presidents before winning the presidency in 1928
choices.textEs: Herbert Hoover, que sirvió en el gabinete de ambos presidentes antes de ganar la presidencia en 1928
choices.explanation: Hoover was in both cabinets, as Secretary of Commerce, and he did win in 1928. Commerce promoted trade and standardisation; it wrote no tax bill.
choices.misconception: assumes the cabinet officer who became president must have held the senior economic post

choices.text: Harry M. Daugherty, the Harding campaign manager who entered the cabinet and resigned under investigation in 1924
choices.textEs: Harry M. Daugherty, el director de campaña de Harding que entró en el gabinete y renunció bajo investigación en 1924
choices.explanation: Daugherty is remembered from this administration and the description fits him — as Attorney General. He ran the Justice Department, which prosecutes; it does not set revenue policy.
choices.misconception: names the best-known figure of the administration's scandals for an economic post

choices.text: Andrew W. Mellon, the Pittsburgh banker who ran the Treasury from 1921 to 1932
choices.textEs: Andrew W. Mellon, el banquero de Pittsburgh que dirigió el Tesoro de 1921 a 1932

items.dokRationale: Recall of one officeholder. The student retrieves a name attached to a department; no weighing of the policy's advantages against its disadvantages is required. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that weighing.
items.explanation: Mellon held the Treasury for eleven years under three presidents, which is why the tax cuts of 1921, 1924, 1926 and 1928 read as one continuous programme rather than as four separate bills — the continuity of the official, not of the presidency, is what made the policy a decade long.
items.explanationEs: Mellon ocupó el Tesoro durante once años bajo tres presidentes, y por eso los recortes fiscales de 1921, 1924, 1926 y 1928 se leen como un solo programa continuo y no como cuatro leyes separadas: la continuidad del funcionario, no de la presidencia, es lo que hizo que la política durara una década.

items.stem: Under President Warren G. Harding's and President Calvin Coolidge's administrations, Americans bought cars, radios and household appliances on installment plans in unprecedented numbers. Why do historians count that credit expansion as a disadvantage of the decade as well as an advantage?
items.stemEs: Durante las administraciones de los presidentes Warren G. Harding y Calvin Coolidge, los estadounidenses compraron automóviles, radios y electrodomésticos a plazos en cantidades sin precedentes. ¿Por qué los historiadores cuentan esa expansión del crédito como una desventaja de la década además de una ventaja?

choices.text: It moved household savings into bank deposits, which the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation then guaranteed against loss
choices.textEs: Trasladó los ahorros de los hogares a depósitos bancarios, que la Corporación Federal de Seguro de Depósitos garantizaba entonces contra pérdidas
choices.explanation: Federal deposit insurance did not exist in the 1920s. The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation was created by the Banking Act of 1933, after thousands of banks had already failed, and an uninsured deposit is one of the decade's real weaknesses.
choices.misconception: places deposit insurance in the decade whose bank failures produced it

choices.text: It let consumption outrun wages, so the decade's demand rested on debt that any downturn in earnings would stop
choices.textEs: Permitió que el consumo superara los salarios, de modo que la demanda de la década se apoyaba en deudas que cualquier caída de los ingresos detendría

choices.text: It raised the real cost of goods, because the carrying charge added to the price of everything bought on time
choices.textEs: Elevaba el costo real de los bienes, porque el cargo financiero se sumaba al precio de todo lo comprado a plazos
choices.explanation: Installment contracts did carry finance charges, so a buyer paid more than the cash price. That is a cost to one household at one purchase; the disadvantage historians weigh is what the aggregate of those contracts did to the economy.
choices.misconception: answers with the price paid by one buyer when asked about the decade's exposure

choices.text: It applied mainly to luxuries, so the great majority of households took on no new debt during the decade
choices.textEs: Se aplicaba principalmente a artículos de lujo, de modo que la gran mayoría de los hogares no asumió nuevas deudas durante la década
choices.explanation: Installment credit financed ordinary durable goods — automobiles, radios, refrigerators, furniture, sewing machines — not luxuries, and it reached ordinary wage-earning households. Treating it as a narrow practice is what makes the decade's debt look harmless.
choices.misconception: shrinks a broad consumer practice to a narrow one so that its risk disappears

items.dokRationale: The student must reason from a mechanism to its consequence: credit raises present demand by committing future income, which is a vulnerability rather than a fact to recall. Naming installment buying as a feature of the 1920s is the DOK 1 version.
items.explanation: Installment credit brought a car or a radio within reach of a household that could not have saved the full price, which is the advantage. The same contract converted future wages into present demand, so a fall in wages stopped new buying and left old payments owing at the same time — the two effects are the same arrangement seen from either end of the decade.
items.explanationEs: El crédito a plazos puso un automóvil o una radio al alcance de un hogar que no habría podido ahorrar el precio completo, y esa es la ventaja. El mismo contrato convertía salarios futuros en demanda presente, de modo que una caída de los salarios detenía las compras nuevas y dejaba pendientes los pagos viejos al mismo tiempo: los dos efectos son el mismo arreglo visto desde cada extremo de la década.

items.stem: President Warren G. Harding's and President Calvin Coolidge's administrations left share trading almost entirely unregulated. Which feature of 1920s stock buying most directly multiplied an investor's losses when prices fell?
items.stemEs: Las administraciones de los presidentes Warren G. Harding y Calvin Coolidge dejaron la compraventa de acciones casi sin regulación alguna. ¿Qué característica de la compra de acciones en los años veinte multiplicaba más directamente las pérdidas de un inversor cuando los precios caían?

choices.text: The Fordney-McCumber Tariff of 1922, which raised duties on imported manufactures to their highest level in American history to that point
choices.textEs: El Arancel Fordney-McCumber de 1922, que elevó los derechos sobre manufacturas importadas a su nivel más alto en la historia estadounidense hasta ese momento
choices.explanation: The tariff is real and it is Harding's, and it did damage farm exports when other countries retaliated. It is an answer about trade policy, not about what happened inside a brokerage account when a share price fell.
choices.misconception: offers a real policy of the same administration in place of the market mechanism asked for

choices.text: Short selling, which the New York Stock Exchange allowed without any federal limit throughout the decade
choices.textEs: La venta en corto, que la Bolsa de Nueva York permitía sin límite federal alguno durante toda la década
choices.explanation: Short selling was permitted and unregulated, so the description is accurate. A short seller profits when prices fall; the question asks what deepened the losses of investors who had bought.
choices.misconception: reaches for the practice that loses money in a rising market, not a falling one

choices.text: Buying on margin, which let an investor borrow most of a share's price and owe the loan in full whatever the share became worth
choices.textEs: La compra a margen, que permitía a un inversor pedir prestada la mayor parte del precio de una acción y deber el préstamo íntegro cualquiera que fuera el valor que alcanzara la acción

choices.text: Installment credit, which financed share purchases in the same way it financed automobiles and radios
choices.textEs: El crédito a plazos, que financiaba la compra de acciones del mismo modo que financiaba automóviles y radios
choices.explanation: Two real forms of 1920s credit, merged. Installment contracts were written by retailers and finance companies for goods a buyer took home; a margin account was a broker's loan against the shares themselves, and the two were not the same arrangement.
choices.misconception: merges consumer installment credit with a brokerage margin loan because both are borrowing

items.dokRationale: The stem asks which of four real features of the period had a specific mechanical effect, so the student must trace what a borrowed stake does to a loss rather than recall that the market was speculative.
items.explanation: A margin loan fixes what the investor owes and leaves the share's value free to move, so a fall takes the whole stake before it touches the lender. The broker's demand for more cash then forces a sale at the worst moment, which is how a falling market turns individual losses into a general one.
items.explanationEs: Un préstamo de margen fija lo que el inversor debe y deja libre el valor de la acción, de modo que una caída consume toda la participación antes de tocar al prestamista. La exigencia de más efectivo por parte del corredor fuerza entonces una venta en el peor momento, y así un mercado a la baja convierte pérdidas individuales en una general.
